rename.from: Post request via fetch gets overriden/replaced in load()
rename.to: Post request via fetch gets overriden/replaced in `load()`

body:
Two options that I can see:

1. Add a hash of the body as an attribute on the `<script type="svelte-data">` containing the inlined response, so that POST requests can be disambiguated
2. only inline GET requests

I prefer 1 over 2 even though 2 is simpler; any reason you can think of that we _shouldn't_ do that?
What sort of hash? I'm assuming we'd have to ship code to the browser to perform the hash?

Apart from the few additional bytes, I personally can't think of anything that speaks against the hash solution, but I also don't have a very deep understanding of all possible requirements that people might have when using POST requests.

One thing from the top of my head: what about POST requests that include files/blobs - could that become a problem?
Possibly... though I don't think there's a good reason anyone would have for POSTing to anything that wasn't a GraphQL endpoint in `load`

I don't really understand the issue. If you have the body to be able to calculate the hash then don't you already have the response? I would think the key would need to be calculated off the request URL or something.

Edit: Ohhh... request body. Not response body. Nevermind

Hashing the post body generally makes sense to me. The one thing that I wonder about is if you're posting a JSON body it could be stringified with the keys in a different order on different executions
It shouldn't be, key enumeration order is standardised. If it _did_ happen like that, it just means SvelteKit would fall back to making the request instead of using the inlined data.

In any case, I don't think it's safe to assume that two requests with different POST bodies would have the same response anyway, even if they happened to be JSON encodings of equivalent objects. That sounds like a place we don't want to go.

issue.title: More detailed explanation of initial_fetch caching
issue.body:
This CL adds some more explanation of how initial_fetch (the client-side "fetch" function in load) caches results *keyed on URL*.

I was really scratching my head when my client-side requests were returning bogus results, even when the server-side was working. It turns out, because I was making requests using parameters passed in the POST request body, semantically different requests to the same URL were getting deduped by svelte's client-side request caching. This documentation change adds a warning about this case, with a bit more detail about how initial_fetch works.

issue.title: load() of index.svelte returns data of _layout.svelte
account for POST bodies when serializing fetches
issue.body:
fixes #633. Figured the pragmatic choice is to ignore requests with a non-string body (as in, they don't get serialized; those fetches are repeated in the client) since other kinds are unlikely in `load` (presumably the main situation where this is useful is with GraphQL, which uses a JSON payload) and it would be undesirable to buffer streams, etc. 

Handling other kinds of bodies is a TODO in any case: https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/blob/7679399ff965760bdf7f44a100087b597d753d9d/packages/kit/src/runtime/server/page/load_node.js#L148-L159

In fact, I think for now it might be best to throw an error if non-string bodies are sent in `fetch` in `load`. Better than silently failing. Though either way it should affect roughly zero people.
